html:
Halloumi is a firm brined cheese of Cyprus, made from goat's and sheep's milk and often cow's milk, which keeps its shape when grilled or fried. Cypriot villages have made it for centuries.

It was a way to keep milk through the hot summer: the curd is cooked in whey, folded with mint and stored in brine. Both Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots, who call it hellim, claim it, and it is one of the few things shared across the divided island. It became the island's largest food export. In 2021 the European Union gave halloumi protected designation of origin status, under a deal meant to cover makers on both sides of the line in Cyprus. Its rise abroad followed the spread of Mediterranean food.
